newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia said to bar Timor meeting speaker.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia said to bar Timor meeting speaker.

text.p: Malaysian immigration authorities barred a Filipino human rights activist from entering the country to speak at a conference on East Timor, the conference organisers said late on Wednesday.

In a statement, the Asia Pacific Conference on East Timor II said Renato Constantino Jr., who had organized the first such conference in Manila in 1994, was stopped by immigration officials at the Kuala Lumpur airport on Wednesday night and not allowed to enter the country.
"I understand he is being sent back by the first flight to the Philippines this morning," Sanusi Osman, a representative of the conference organisers, told Reuters on Thursday.

Constantino was scheduled to speak at the conference, to be held here November 9- 12. Conference organisers said they sent lawyers to negotiate with the immigration officers, but failed to gain Constantino's entry.

A statement the organisers attributed to Constantino said: "This latest act of suppression can only spur us, advocates of the right to self-determination of the East Timorese, to continue the struggle with more resolve..."
The Malaysian government on Wednesday said it has advised the group not to go ahead with the meeting, but stopped short of saying it was banned.

Malaysia opposes the conference for fear of harming its ties with Indonesia, which invaded East Timor in December 1975 and annexed the Portuguese colony the next year. The United Nations still recognises Lisbon as the administering authority for the territory.

Sanusi reiterated on Thursday that the group would go ahead with the conference. He said more attendees were expected to arrive in the next few days, and that the group wanted to avoid any more run-ins with immigration authorities.
"We have to do something," Sanusi said. "We will have our people at the airport."
Some 200 people from 24 countries and 75 organisations plan to attend the meeting at a Kuala Lumpur hotel, organisers said.

Local journalists said Deputy Home Minister Megat Junid Megat Ayob asked them at a closed-door meeting on Wednesday not to report on the conference, but said the government would not stop the meeting or keep foreign journalists from covering it.
